mainTopic: Liability for a תולדה done together with its אב, and the role of intention when throwing on שבת
overview: On the previous amud, רב יהודה said in שמואל's name that רבי obligates two liabilities when one act involves both הוצאה (an אב) and הכנסה (its תולדה). The גמרא asks how this can be, since רבי counts exactly thirty-nine מלאכות from a פסוק. רב יוסף answers that the statement was really taught on רבי יהודה's view, in a case where an object is thrown from רשות היחיד into רשות הרבים and travels four אמות there. The גמרא then tests whether רבי יהודה obligates two in that case. Each proof is pushed off: the throwing case may be about קלוטה כמה שהונחה, and the weaving case of שובט and מדקדק may be about whether they are אבות or תולדות. רבה and רב יוסף settle it: רבי יהודה obligates only one. רבינא and רב אשי then discuss how a thrower's intended landing spot affects liability. The גמרא applies this to throwing farther or shorter than intended, and questions the comparison to writing שם from שמעון. The amud ends with a new ברייתא about throwing between two public domains with a private domain in the middle.

steps.title: Does רבי really give liability for a sub-category done with its main category?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the claim that רבי makes someone liable for a תולדה when it happens together with its own אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are we really saying that רבי holds a person liable for a sub-category of labor when it is done together with its main category?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by the earlier ruling and asks whether it really reflects רבי's opinion. This line sets up the challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier statement, from the previous amud, is רב יהודה's claim that רבי obligates two: one for הוצאה (taking out) and one for הכנסה (bringing in). These are an אב and its own תולדה. The גמרא doubts that רבי would give a separate liability for the תולדה when it is done together with its אב.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a formula expressing surprise at an implication)
A sub-category (derivative) of a main labor
A main category of labor (אב מלאכה)
Together with (in the place of) its own main category

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabbi holds liable
for a sub-category in the place of (together with) its main category?
phrases.notes: The case in question is הוצאה (an אב) together with הכנסה (its תולדה).

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דִּמְחַיֵּיב רַבִּי אַתּוֹלָדָה בִּמְקוֹם אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the implication of an earlier statement in the sugya, which comes on the previous amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is it really רבי's view that a תולדה done together with its own אב brings a separate liability?

steps.title: רבי counts exactly thirty-nine labors from a verse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי deriving exactly thirty-nine מלאכות from the words of a פסוק, which seems to contradict the earlier claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי says, from the words 'things', 'the things', and 'these are the things', we learn the thirty-nine labors that were told to משה at סיני!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its doubt. רבי counts the forbidden labors as exactly thirty-nine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי derives the number from the wording of the פסוק. 'Things' is plural, so it means two. 'The' adds one more, making three. The letters of אלה add up to thirty-six, for a total of thirty-nine. If רבי works with a fixed count of main categories, it is hard to see him giving a separate liability for a sub-category done in the same act as its own main category. So רבי seems to contradict the earlier statement attributed to him.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a contradicting source)
'These are the things' (שמות ל״ה:א׳), the פסוק that introduces the שבת laws
The thirty-nine forbidden labors of שבת
Were told to משה at סיני

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי is denying that הכנסה counts as a forbidden labor at all. The question is only whether a sub-category done in the same act as its own main category adds a second, separate liability.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi says:
'Things', 'the things', 'these are the things' —
these are the thirty-nine labors
that were told to Moses at Sinai!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source that gives the question of step 1 its force.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier statement attributing to רבי a separate liability for a תולדה done together with its אב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי counts a fixed number of thirty-nine main labors. That suggests a sub-category done in the same act as its own main category does not add a second liability, so the earlier statement contradicts רבי's own view.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the ruling belongs to רבי יהודה, not רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the contradiction only arises if the statement is attributed to רבי. He attributes it to רבי יהודה, so there is no difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: You, Master, teach that statement about this (רבי), so you have a contradiction between רבי and רבי. We teach it about רבי יהודה, so we have no difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף solves the problem by changing whose opinion the earlier statement represents. He says it was never רבי's view; it belongs to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction depended entirely on the earlier ruling being in רבי's name. רב יוסף teaches רב יהודה's 'two liabilities' statement on רבי יהודה's case instead (step 4), so there is no clash with רבי's count of thirty-nine. Whether רבי יהודה really obligates two is examined in the steps that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the difficulty
'Master', a respectful way of addressing the questioner
Teaches it (attributes the statement)
רבי against רבי (one statement of the same Sage contradicting another)
We teach / we learn it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא. Instead of reconciling two statements, it changes the attribution of one of them, and the contradiction disappears.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
The Master teaches it with regard to this (Rabbi),
and so he has a difficulty of Rabbi against Rabbi.
We teach it with regard to Rabbi Yehuda —
and it is not difficult for us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: מָר אַהָא מַתְנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-attribution of the statement to a different Sage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier ruling was רבי's opinion, so it clashed with his count of thirty-nine labors.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling is רבי יהודה's opinion, so there is no contradiction within רבי.

steps.title: ברייתא: רבי יהודה holds the thrower liable
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה holds a person liable when he throws from רשות היחיד to רשות הרבים and the object travels four אמות there, while the חכמים exempt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: one who throws from the private domain to the public domain, and the object passed four cubits in the public domain, רבי יהודה holds him liable and the חכמים exempt him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רב יוסף's answer. It shows a ברייתא where רבי יהודה rules on exactly this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא is a different case from the one the earlier statement was taught on in רבי's name (הוצאה plus הכנסה). Here the object is taken out into public and also travels four אמות there. רבי יהודה holds the person liable and the חכמים exempt him. רב יוסף teaches the 'two liabilities' statement on this case instead, so רבי is never involved. The ברייתא itself just says מחייב, and the next steps argue whether that means two (שמואל) or only one (רבה and רב יוסף).

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a supporting source)
Private domain
Public domain
Four cubits, the distance that makes carrying in public a forbidden labor
Exempt (from liability)

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף teaches רב יהודה's 'two liabilities' statement on רבי יהודה's case (הוצאה plus four אמות in public), not on רבי's case (הוצאה plus הכנסה). This avoids a clash with רבי's count of exactly thirty-nine מלאכות. Step 12 will show that רבה and רב יוסף hold רבי יהודה actually obligates only one.

phrases.english: As it was taught: from the private domain to the public domain
and it passed four cubits in the public domain —
Rabbi Yehuda holds him liable
and the Rabbis exempt him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's re-attribution with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that the liability ruling belongs to רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי יהודה holds the thrower liable in this exact case and the חכמים exempt him

steps.title: שמואל: רבי יהודה obligates two sin-offerings
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: in the throwing case, רבי יהודה obligates two חטאות, one for הוצאה and one for העברה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: רבי יהודה would obligate him two sin-offerings, one for carrying out and one for moving the object four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's explanation of the ברייתא from step 4. According to שמואל, רבי יהודה obligates the thrower two קרבנות, not one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking an object out from רשות היחיד to רשות הרבים is הוצאה, which is an אב. Moving it four אמות in רשות הרבים is העברה, which is treated here as its תולדה. If רבי יהודה obligates two, he holds a person liable for a תולדה done together with its אב.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying an object out from one domain to another
Moving an object four אמות within רשות הרבים
Holds liable (here, to bring a חטאת)
Two (two separate חטאות)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the base statement the גמרא will use as its proof. The next steps first defend it and then challenge it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Rabbi Yehuda would obligate him two [sin-offerings]
phrases.notes: In the case of throwing from a private domain to a public domain, where the object traveled four cubits.

phrases.english: one for carrying out
and one for moving [four cubits]

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מְחַיֵּיב הָיָה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interprets the ברייתא from step 4 to show that רבי יהודה obligates two, which supports the idea of liability for a תולדה done together with its אב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, רבי יהודה obligates two חטאות in the throwing case: one for הוצאה and one for העברה.

steps.title: Why שמואל's reading must be two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves שמואל's reading. If רבי יהודה obligated only one, the חכמים would exempt completely, and that cannot be, since the person did carry out from רשות היחיד to רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you thought רבי יהודה obligates only one, then by implication the Rabbis exempt him completely? But he took it out from the private domain to the public domain!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא must be read as two קרבנות for רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the חכמים exempt. If רבי יהודה obligated only one, the חכמים would be exempting a plain act of הוצאה, and that makes no sense. So the חכמים must exempt only the extra העברה, while רבי יהודה obligates for both acts.

keyTerms.meaning: For if it would enter your mind
By implication
They exempt completely
He took out

phrases.english: For if it would enter your mind
that he obligates only one,
then by implication the Rabbis exempt completely?
But he took it out
from the private domain to the public domain!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ חֲדָא הוּא דִּמְחַיֵּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the logic behind שמואל's reading of 'two'.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה obligates two in the throwing case, and is therefore liable for a תולדה together with its אב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A reductio: if רבי יהודה obligated only one, the חכמים would be exempting a clear act of הוצאה.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יהודה obligates only one after all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Perhaps רבי יהודה obligates one and the חכמים exempt completely, in a case where the person intended the object to land as soon as it entered רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps I can really tell you that רבי יהודה obligates only one and the Rabbis exempt completely. How can that happen? When he said: as soon as it goes out into the public domain, let it land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by describing a different case, where the חכמים could exempt completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the claim that the חכמים could never fully exempt someone who carried out. The גמרא answers that they could, if the thrower wanted the object to land right at the edge of רשות הרבים and it flew farther instead. In that case the single liability of רבי יהודה is for הוצאה, not for two acts.

keyTerms.meaning: From where [do you know]?
Perhaps actually
And how do you find such a case?
Let it come to rest

phrases.english: From where [do you know]? Perhaps I can really tell you
that Rabbi Yehuda obligates only one,
and the Rabbis exempt completely,
and how do you find such a case?
For example, where he said:

phrases.aramaic: עַד דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים תְּנוּחַ.
phrases.english: As soon as it goes out into the public domain, let it land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of steps 5 and 6 by describing a case where the חכמים can exempt completely.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the ברייתא proves רבי יהודה obligates two.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the חכמים could not exempt completely. But in a case where the person intended the object to land immediately upon entering רשות הרבים, they could.

steps.title: The dispute is about whether an object in the air counts as landed
steps.stepSummary: In that case, the dispute is whether an object in the air counts as resting (קלוטה כמה שהונחה). רבי יהודה says yes, so the person's intention was fulfilled. The חכמים say no. So רבי יהודה does not obligate for a תולדה together with its אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what they disagree about. רבי יהודה holds: we say an object in the air is like one that has landed, so his intention was fulfilled. The Rabbis hold: we do not say an object in the air is like one that has landed, so his intention was not fulfilled. But for a subcategory together with a primary category, רבי יהודה does not obligate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the rejection by explaining what רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the moment the object entered the air of רשות הרבים it counted as landed, just as the person intended, so he is liable once for הוצאה. For the חכמים, it only landed farther away, which is not what he intended, so he is fully exempt. On this reading the ברייתא says nothing about a תולדה together with its אב.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what they disagree about
An object held in the air counts as if it has landed
His intention was fulfilled
A subcategory done together with its primary category

steps.confusionAlert: This explanation of קלוטה is not saying the person is liable for the extra four אמות. The single liability is only for הוצאה, which counts as complete the moment the object enters the air.

phrases.english: And this is what they disagree about: Rabbi Yehuda holds:
We say an object in the air is like one that has landed,
and so his intention was fulfilled.
And the Rabbis hold:
We do not say an object in the air is like one that has landed,
and so his intention was not fulfilled!
But for a subcategory together with a primary category
Rabbi Yehuda does not obligate.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי, דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: אָמְרִינַן קְלוּטָה כְּמָה שֶׁהוּנְּחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection by naming the principle behind the dispute in the case from step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the throwing ברייתא is fully neutralized.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute could be about קלוטה כמה שהונחה rather than about liability for a תולדה together with its אב.

steps.title: Proof from lining up and beating threads
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this and brings a ברייתא: רבי יהודה adds שובט and מדקדק to the list of מלאכות, while the חכמים say these fall under מיסך and אורג. The גמרא infers the case is one where both were done together, which would show liability for a תולדה with its אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot enter your mind, as it was taught: רבי יהודה adds also lining up the threads and beating them. They said to him: lining up is included in stretching the warp, and beating is included in weaving. Is it not talking about one who did both together? Learn from this that רבי יהודה would obligate for a subcategory together with its primary category!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא refuses to accept that רבי יהודה does not obligate for a תולדה with its אב. It brings a new ברייתא as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say שובט and מדקדק are only תולדות of מיסך and אורג. The גמרא assumes the person did each one together with its אב. If so, רבי יהודה's adding them means he obligates an extra קרבן for the תולדה even when done with its אב.

keyTerms.meaning: Lining up the warp threads (separating them with a rod)
Beating the woof threads tight
Stretching the warp threads on the loom (an אב מלאכה)
Weaving (an אב מלאכה)
Is it not? (introduces an inference)
Together with each other

phrases.english: That cannot enter your mind, as it was taught [in a baraita]:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מוֹסִיף אַף הַשּׁוֹבֵט וְהַמְדַקְדֵּק.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda adds also lining up and beating [the threads].

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: שׁוֹבֵט הֲרֵי הוּא בִּכְלַל מֵיסֵךְ,
phrases.english: They said to him: lining up is included in stretching the warp,
and beating is included in weaving.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו דְּעַבְדִינְהוּ לְתַרְוַויְיהוּ בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי,
phrases.english: Is it not that he did both of them together,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מְחַיֵּיב הָיָה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: and learn from it that Rabbi Yehuda would obligate
for a subcategory together with its primary category!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מוֹסִיף אַף הַשּׁוֹבֵט וְהַמְדַקְדֵּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion of step 8 by bringing a new ברייתא that seems to show רבי יהודה does obligate for a תולדה with its אב.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה obligates for a תולדה done together with its אב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא where רבי יהודה adds שובט and מדקדק, read as a case where each was done together with its אב.

steps.title: Maybe they argue only whether these are primary categories
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Perhaps each act was done alone, and the dispute is only whether שובט and מדקדק are אבות (רבי יהודה) or תולדות (the חכמים).
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps it really means he did this one alone and that one alone, and רבי יהודה does not obligate for a subcategory together with its primary category. And this is what they disagree about: רבי יהודה holds these are primary categories, and the Rabbis hold these are subcategories.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from the weaving ברייתא by reading it as a case where each act was done separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on assuming the acts were done together. If they were done separately, the dispute is not about extra liability at all. It is only about status: רבי יהודה counts שובט and מדקדק as their own אבות, while the חכמים count them as תולדות. So again there is no proof about a תולדה done with its אב.

keyTerms.meaning: By itself, alone
Primary categories of מלאכה
Subcategories of מלאכה
They are

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs that רבי יהודה obligates for a תולדה together with its אב are pushed off. The throwing case may be about קלוטה כמה שהונחה. The weaving case may be about whether שובט and מדקדק are אבות or תולדות.

phrases.english: From where [do you know]? Perhaps it really means
that he did this one alone and that one alone,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַתּוֹלָדָה בִּמְקוֹם אָב לָא מְחַיֵּיב,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda does not obligate for a subcategory together with its primary category,
and this is what they disagree about:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר הָנֵי אָבוֹת נִינְהוּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds these are primary categories,
and the Rabbis hold these are subcategories.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא לְעוֹלָם דְּעַבְדַּהּ לְהָא לְחוּדַּהּ וְהָא לְחוּדַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 9 by reading the ברייתא as a case of separate acts.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the שובט and מדקדק ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the acts were done together. They may have been done separately, so the dispute is only whether these acts are אבות or תולדות.

steps.title: The word 'adds' shows שובט and מדקדק are main categories
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the rejection in Step 10. The ברייתא says רבי יהודה 'adds', which only makes sense if he is adding new אבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can know this is so, because the ברייתא says 'רבי יהודה adds.' If you say he means they are main categories, 'adds' makes sense: he adds main categories. But if you say they are only sub-categories, what is he 'adding'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the idea from Step 10 that the argument is about whether שובט and מדקדק are אבות. It points to the wording of the ברייתא as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the 39 אבות מלאכות, and רבי יהודה 'adds' to that list. Adding to a list of main categories means adding new main categories. Sub-categories were never on the list, so 'adding' them would mean nothing. So the ברייתא is not about doing a תולדה together with its אב, and Step 9's proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Know it (a word that brings support for a claim)
Adds (to the list of מלאכות)
Main categories of forbidden work
Sub-categories that come from a main category
If you say, it works well

phrases.english: Know that it is so, for it teaches: 'Rabbi Yehuda adds.'
Granted, if you say they are main categories,
what does 'he adds' mean? He adds main categories.
But if you say they are sub-categories,
what is he adding?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in Step 10 with the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא's dispute is about whether שובט and מדקדק are אבות or תולדות

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף: רבי יהודה obligates only one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a statement from רבה and רב יוסף. Both say רבי יהודה obligates only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבה and רב יוסף both said, 'רבי יהודה obligated only one חטאת.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion. It brings two אמוראים who say outright that רבי יהודה obligates only one חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5 through 11 went back and forth. Each proof that רבי יהודה obligates two for a תולדה with its אב (steps 6 and 9) was pushed off (steps 7-8 and 10-11). Now an explicit statement settles it: one חטאת only. This goes against שמואל's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (an אמורא statement that supports the point)
Both of them
One (חטאת)

steps.whatToRemember: The final view: רבי יהודה obligates only one חטאת. He does not obligate separately for a תולדה done together with its אב.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rabba and Rav Yosef both said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא חִיֵּיב רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶלָּא אַחַת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda obligated only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the direction of Step 11 with an explicit אמורא statement.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה obligates only one חטאת.

steps.title: רבינא: How could he be liable twice if he wanted only one landing spot?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי about the original idea that רבי יהודה obligates two. The thrower wanted the object to land in only one place, so how can he be liable for two landings?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: According to what we first thought, that רבי יהודה obligated two, how does that work? If he wanted it to land here (right at the start of רשות הרבים), he did not want it to land there (four אמות in). And if he wanted it to land there, he did not want it to land here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא looks back at the first assumption, that רבי יהודה obligates two חטאות. He asks how that could ever work given what the thrower intended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two חטאות would be for carrying out into רשות הרבים and for moving four אמות inside it. Each one needs the object to land where he wanted. But a person intends one landing spot, not two. So at least one of the two acts was not done as he intended.

keyTerms.meaning: What we first had in mind
He wants it (to land there)
Two (חטאות)

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
And according to what we first had in mind,
that Rabbi Yehuda obligated two, how could that be?
If he wanted it here (at the start of the public domain),
he did not want it here (four cubits in).
If he wanted it here (four cubits in),
he did not want it here (at the start).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: וּלְמַאי דִּסְלֵיק אַדַּעְתִּין מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first assumption (two חטאות) that Step 12 rejected and asks how it could even work.
steps.kashyaTarget: The original assumption that רבי יהודה obligates two חטאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Liability needs the thrower's intention to be fulfilled, and he can intend only one landing spot, not two.

steps.title: רב אשי: He said 'let it land wherever it lands'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the thrower said, 'Wherever it lands, let it land.' So any landing spot fulfills what he wanted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is a case where the thrower said, 'Any place it wants to land, let it land.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא's question. The case is one where the thrower did not care where the object landed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the thrower is happy with any landing spot, both acts match his intention. So the two-חטאות view could work in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Wherever it wants, let it land
In a case where he says

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is where he says, 'Any place it wants, let it land.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּאוֹמֵר ״כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁתִּרְצֶה — תָּנוּחַ״
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A thrower always intends one specific landing spot, so two liabilities are impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: If he said 'let it land anywhere,' every landing spot matches his intention.

steps.title: Obvious: intending eight and throwing four makes him liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new topic. If someone meant to throw eight אמות but threw only four, he is clearly liable, like someone who wrote שם as part of שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that if he intended to throw eight אמות and threw four, he is liable. It is like someone who wrote שם, the first part of שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion about intention when throwing. It starts with a case it calls obvious, and this sets up the real question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who meant to write שמעון but stopped after שם is still liable, because שם is a real word on its way to שמעון. The same seems true here: four אמות is part of the way to eight. So he did part of what he planned, and that part is a full מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
He intended to throw
The word שם, written as part of the name שמעון

phrases.english: It is obvious: if he intended to throw eight cubits
and threw four, he is liable,
for this is like writing 'Shem' from 'Shimon.'

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא נִתְכַּוֵּון לִזְרוֹק שְׁמֹנֶה וְזָרַק אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related new topic about intention in throwing, building on the theme of intention from Steps 13 and 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intending eight אמות and throwing four makes him liable, like writing שם from שמעון.

steps.title: The question: intending four and throwing eight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the reverse case. If he meant to throw four אמות but the object went eight, is he liable?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he intended to throw four אמות and threw eight, what is the law? Do we say, 'Well, he moved it'? Or do we say, 'It did not land where he wanted'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the real question, the reverse of the obvious case. It lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side: he did move the object four אמות and more, so he did the forbidden act. The other side: it landed at eight, not at four where he wanted, so his plan was never carried out.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the law?
Do we say this, or perhaps that?
He did carry it out
It did not come to rest (there)

phrases.aramaic: נִתְכַּוֵּון לִזְרוֹק אַרְבַּע וְזָרַק שְׁמֹנֶה — מַהוּ?
phrases.english: If he intended to throw four and threw eight, what is the law?
Do we say: he did carry it out,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא: הֵיכָא דְּבָעֵי, הָא לָא נָח.
phrases.english: or perhaps: where he wanted it, it did not land?

steps.triggerLanguage: נִתְכַּוֵּון לִזְרוֹק אַרְבַּע וְזָרַק שְׁמֹנֶה — מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the obvious case to the reverse case, which is in doubt.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a thrower liable when the object goes farther than he intended?

steps.title: This is רבינא's question, and רב אשי already answered it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this is the same question רבינא asked. רב אשי's answer was that he is liable only if he said 'let it land anywhere.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this exactly what רבינא asked רב אשי? And רב אשי answered: it is where he said, 'Any place it wants, let it land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing back to רבינא and רב אשי. Their exchange already settles it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's question assumed that if the object lands somewhere he did not want, he is not liable. That is why רב אשי needed the case of 'let it land anywhere.' So intending four and throwing eight makes him liable only if he said that.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't this the same thing as

phrases.aramaic: וְלָאו הַיְינוּ דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: But isn't this what Ravina said to Rav Ashi,
and he answered him:
It is where he says, 'Any place it wants, let it land.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו הַיְינוּ דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 using the exchange in Steps 13 and 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is not liable unless he said 'wherever it lands, let it land.'
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this is a brand-new answer. It repeats רב אשי's words from Step 14 and applies them to the new question.

steps.title: The comparison to writing שם from שמעון does not hold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back and attacks the 'obvious' case. Writing שמעון requires writing שם first, but throwing eight אמות does not require first landing at four.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what you said, that it is like writing שם from שמעון, is it really the same? There, until he writes שם, he cannot write שמעון. Here, is it true that until it is thrown four אמות, it cannot be thrown eight?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison it used in Step 15. This shows the 'obvious' case is not obvious after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In writing, שם is a necessary first part of שמעון, so writing it is a real step in his plan. In throwing, an object flies to eight אמות without ever landing at four. So landing at four is not a step in his plan of eight, and he may not be liable. The question is left without an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really comparable?
There … here (setting two cases side by side)
Eight (אמות)

steps.whatToRemember: Intending eight and throwing four turns out to be in doubt too. It differs from writing שם from שמעון, because a throw never has to stop at four on its way to eight.

phrases.aramaic: וּדְקָאָמְרַתְּ הֲרֵי כָּתַב ״שֵׁם״ מִשִּׁמְעוֹן, מִי דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: And what you said, that it is like writing 'Shem' from 'Shimon': is it comparable?
There, as long as 'Shem' is not written,
'Shimon' cannot be written.
Here, as long as it is not thrown four,
can it not be thrown eight?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְקָאָמְרַתְּ הֲרֵי כָּתַב ״שֵׁם״ מִשִּׁמְעוֹן, מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to Step 15 and challenges its comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison in Step 15 between throwing four of eight and writing שם from שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שם is a necessary part of writing שמעון, but landing at four is not a necessary part of throwing eight. So the comparison fails.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that being liable for part of a planned act depends on whether that part is a real step toward the whole act.

steps.title: Throwing between two public domains through a private domain
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one who throws from רשות הרבים to רשות הרבים, with a רשות היחיד in the middle, is חייב if the throw covers four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone throws an object from one רשות הרבים to another רשות הרבים, and a רשות היחיד is in between, he is חייב if it covers four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new ברייתא about throwing across a private area that sits between two public areas. The ruling is that four אמות of distance makes him חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person is חייב for moving an object four אמות within רשות הרבים. Here the throw is split into two parts by a רשות היחיד in the middle. The ברייתא teaches that the two public-domain parts add up together. The private area in between does not break the four אמות into separate pieces.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this introduces a ברייתא
Public domain
Private domain
In the middle
Four cubits; the minimum distance for liability when carrying in a public domain
Liable

steps.confusionAlert: He is not made חייב here for bringing the object into or out of the רשות היחיד. His liability comes from the four אמות counted in the two public areas together.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question of whether two separate stretches of רשות הרבים can combine to make four אמות. The following lines of the sugya will explore that.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who throws from the public domain to the public domain
and a private domain is in the middle,
four cubits: he is liable,
phrases.notes: The distance in both public areas is counted together

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן הַזּוֹרֵק מֵרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא and topic after the discussion of throwing eight versus four אמות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When someone throws from one רשות הרבים to another through a רשות היחיד, he is חייב if the throw covers four אמות in total.
